proposition: Chapter 50 is named Detroit Zoning Ordinance
Chapter enacted pursuant to state powers and limits including two named acts
Chapter applies to all City land unless exempt from local zoning
Chapter guides and regulates land use and development for public welfare
Classify land by suitability for uses
Regulate location construction reconstruction alteration and use
Ensure light air privacy safety and access
Conserve or enhance property values
Protect City areas from incompatible-use encroachment
Prevent building overcrowding of land
Avoid undue population congestion
Establish reasonable conformity standards
Lessen street congestion through off-street parking and loading
Facilitate adequate public requirements
Provide elimination of nonconforming structures and uses
Promote visual environment through development and civic design
Protect resources and ensure environmental-law consistency
Define administrative powers and duties
Provide penalties for Chapter violations and amendments
Provide BZA and its powers and duties
Unless otherwise stated Chapter provisions are minimum requirements serving named purposes
Approximate mapped boundaries follow named lines or their extensions unless otherwise shown
competency_test: mapped approximation resolves to qualifying line

proposition: Unsubdivided parallel strip dimensions are measured at right angles with mapped frontage
PDD must interpret uncertain contradictory or conflicting mapped boundary by spirit and purpose
competency_test: requires discretionary finding; no deterministic outcome

proposition: Vacated right-of-way joins adjoining districts; former centerline divides differing districts
competency_test: same districts absorb all; differing districts split centerline

proposition: More restrictive Chapter or state/federal rule controls to extent permitted by law
More restrictive rule controls internal or City Code conflict
Article VIII-XI use lists override conflicting Article XII use-table marking or omission
competency_test: list controls C R or blank conflict

proposition: Chapter does not intend to disturb private land agreements
Chapter controls when more restrictive than private agreement
Private agreement controls when more restrictive than Chapter
City has no responsibility to monitor or enforce private agreements
Prior-ordinance violation continues unless activity complies with Chapter
Prior legal nonconformity continues while originating situation exists
Prior nonconformity becoming conforming under Chapter loses nonconforming status
Valid May 28 2005 approvals survive to expiration and permit then-current standards while valid and un-lapsed
Uses valid May 28 2005 remain valid under authorizing terms and controls
Chapter requires no change to structure plans construction or use with pre-effective-date building permit
Original body may grant one extension up to one year if approval findings remain valid
competency_test: 12 months first extension allowed; second or 13 months denied

proposition: Reapplication after expired project approval uses standards at reapplication
Complete pre-May-28 application pending at enactment may at applicant option use prior ordinance wholly
Approved opted project uses standards when complete application submitted
Reapplication for expired permit uses standards at reapplication
Project without accepted-complete pre-effective application is subject to all Chapter requirements
competency_test: missing timely accepted-complete application selects Chapter

proposition: Invalidity ruling leaves remaining portions unaffected
Each portion would have been adopted regardless of invalidity of others
Sections reserved
